source_refs.note: Topic 27.5.2 as printed (PDF 174): the book's paragraph, Figure 27.16 (redrawn) and the three run-in paragraphs on mRNA, rRNA and tRNA.

blocks.text: RNA is usually single stranded unlike DNA, but the chain can fold back to itself to form a helical loop. A ribonucleotide chain in the RNA contains ribose, four nitrogenous bases (A, U, G, and C), and the phosphate group as given in Figure 27.16. There are three major types of RNA in the cells.

blocks.alt: A single RNA strand drawn as a helical ribbon, with bases sticking out from it, each labelled A, U, G or C.
blocks.caption: Figure 27.16: Structure of RNA (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 27.16).

blocks.text: Messenger RNA (mRNA): it carries the genetic blueprint copied from the DNA in the nucleus.
Ribosomal RNA (rRNA): it helps to make up the ribosome.
Transfer RNA (tRNA): it translates the nucleotide sequence in mRNA into the corresponding sequence of amino acids in a protein.
